translated_text: Paris, December 25, 1940. My darling, I'm not bad, I didn't write to you yesterday because, on the one hand, I was sick, and on the other hand, I had a lot of work—I was sick, well, I had a little attack, but very little. I didn't even stay in bed, and today I'm much, much better! Yesterday I went to see a great specialist, who took an X-ray and told me some important things; that it's not the lungs that produce the microbes, but the liver (Leber) and the intestines (Decarme), the bacilli, and that the source needs to be treated. But that it's not serious at all, and in a month it will all be over! I have to go back to him next Saturday with 1 kilogram of Bismuth in my stomach (Bron), and he's going to repeat the examination before giving me the exact diet (Diet) to follow. Finally, he's a serious man (his prices reflect that: 300 francs for the radio, 60 for each visit). I trust him. I hope he'll cure me. Work is still going badly; I'm always busy buying lab equipment and waiting for Winkler, who's never available. I haven't heard from you. Maybe tonight. I didn't have that letter receipt from dear Bobchen. If I had work, I would go. I don't have time. Since I don't want to think when I'm here, I'm not left alone for a minute, and when I'm home, I'm too tired. I'm a little afraid of Sundays; I have to find something for those days. I called Spira. He wasn't there. I have to call again this afternoon. My darling, I promise to write to you every day now, same thing. I adore you and kiss you and I miss you terribly, your Baba- PARIS RP 15 30 26-IV 1940 D ART AVIATION IS THE MOST BEAUTIFUL OF CAREERS Robert Zweigenthal 10 1st Reg. Vel Rofeen D DE SP 2.197 40 AULT V
